memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: So the Lord scattered them from there over all the earth, and they stopped building the city. That is why it was called Babel - because there the Lord confused the language of the whole world. From there the Lord scattered them over the face of the whole earth. - Gen 11:8-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The tower stands unfinished. The builders scatter. The place is named Babel - "confusion." Human pride has collapsed, and the great project that was to make their name famous instead became a byword for failure. What people build to exalt themselves rarely ends the way they imagine.

But look closer, and something remarkable emerges. The scattering they most feared (v.4) is exactly what God had commanded in the first place - to fill the earth (Gen 9:1). What felt like judgement was also God accomplishing His good purpose. He scattered them into the calling they had refused. Even God's judgements serve His larger plan for the world.

This is such a comfort. God's purposes are never defeated by human rebellion. When we resist His will, He is able to work through even our failures to bring about what He intended all along. Our pride cannot outmanoeuvre His plan.

And the story does not end at Babel. What was scattered there begins to be gathered in Christ. At Pentecost, the curse was gloriously reversed - people of every language heard the wonders of God in their own tongue (Acts 2:5-11). And at the end, a countless multitude "from every nation, tribe, people and language" will stand together before the throne (Rev 7:9). Babel scattered; Christ gathers. The confusion of human pride is answered by the unity of divine grace.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Have you seen God work His purposes even through your failures?
- How does Pentecost's reversal of Babel encourage you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Sovereign God, thank You that human pride cannot defeat Your purposes, and that You work even through our failures. Thank You that what Babel scattered, Christ gathers. Gather me into Your people.
Amen.
